sentence: This project tests how ketamine affects the opioid system by looking at both short-term and long-term effects.
This project builds a non-invasive method that uses magnetic resonance imaging and computational fluid dynamics to measure coronary fractional flow reserve.
This project develops tests that measure how CRISPR-mediated excision of pathogenic alleles affects neurons and glia in animal models.
This project provides animal care and support for cancer research that uses animal models such as mice and rats.
This project studies how cocaine changes the proteins at synapses in the nucleus accumbens and how this relates to drug-seeking and relapse.
This project builds a system that uses machine learning to read the output of retinal ganglion cells in blind retinas of animal models.
This project develops computational tools to speed up genetic discovery in mouse models of human disease and studies genetic factors behind lymphoma and diabetes.
This project tries to find rare gene variants that cause lupus in familial and childhood-onset patients and studies what these variants do.
This project studies whether fusion oncoproteins in pediatric leukemias form molecular condensates and how condensates relate to gene regulation.
This project uses machine learning on ventilator waveform and health record data to find which patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome gain from paralytic medications.
This project studies how a group of neurons and peptides in the prelimbic cortex affect binge drinking behavior.
This project studies how activating and repressive complexes compete to set gene expression levels by changing chromatin structure.
This project tries to make chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapies for HIV last longer and work better in the nonhuman primate model.
This project studies the epigenetic mechanisms behind how prostate cancer undergoes neuroendocrine transdifferentiation.
This project builds a disease simulation model to judge the benefits and harms of using artificial intelligence-assisted tools to screen for oral cancer.
This project studies the roles of the epigenome in uterine leiomyoma using patient-derived tissue explants and cellular models.
This project studies how chromatin passes on the state of hematopoietic stem cells and how this affects their self-renewal and differentiation.
This project tests a coating that reduces scarring and inflammation around cochlear implants.
This project studies how overactivity of the mechanistic target of rapamycin pathway causes brain malformation and epilepsy in a 3-D human neural cell culture model.
This project builds an artificial intelligence-based MRI method to study brain metabolism in people living with HIV and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
